name: benchmark-validity
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases benchmark:1,2,21,63,66.
prompt: Our Go 1.24 parsing benchmark reports 0.3 ns/op. It uses a b.N loop, ignores the result, and reuses a reader across iterations. How should we establish a valid baseline?

assertions.text: Investigates elimination and consumed input without claiming timing alone proves a cause.
Recommends valid b.Loop usage or a justified b.N benchmark with observable work and excluded setup.
Keeps fixture and benchmark definitions identical across comparisons and reports allocations.

name: inconclusive-comparison
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases benchmark:4,5,12.
prompt: benchstat shows Parse at 4.592 us/op versus 4.481 us/op, ~ (p=0.089 n=10), with wide intervals. Can we claim a 2.4% improvement and omit the ~ row?

assertions.text: Calls the timing comparison inconclusive and retains the row.
Does not claim equivalence or rerun until significant.
Proposes noise control and a predeclared follow-up if the practical decision warrants it.

name: serial-candidates
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases benchmark:50,81.
prompt: Three agents implemented competing optimizations in worktrees on the same VM. Can they each run benchmarks concurrently against their own fresh baseline?

assertions.text: Requires serial measurement on shared hardware.
Compares candidates against the same baseline and controlled environment.
Distinguishes independent implementation from measurement and addresses winner selection bias.

name: toolchain-confound
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases benchmark:1; performance:3.
prompt: Baseline was Go 1.24 on a laptop, candidate Go 1.26 on CI. Candidate is 12% faster. Write the conclusion for our code optimization.

assertions.text: Declines to attribute the difference to the code.
Requires rebuilding baseline and candidate on the same toolchain and hardware with matched flags and workload.
Labels current evidence unverified or incomparable.

name: external-wait
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases benchmark:11,31; performance:2.
prompt: Our Go API p99 is 800ms with low CPU. Most distributed trace time is a database request, and many goroutines are waiting on database/sql. Should we first pool handler buffers?

assertions.text: Investigates external latency, connection waits and query behavior before allocation tuning.
Uses waiting or trace evidence rather than treating a CPU profile as the full latency budget.
Does not assert goroutine stacks alone prove the database server is the cause.

name: allocation-versus-retention
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases benchmark:7,22; performance:9,59.
prompt: CPU is dominated by mallocgc and GC. alloc_space climbs steadily but inuse_space after comparable GCs stays flat. Is this a memory leak? What should we optimize?

assertions.text: Separates cumulative allocation churn from retained heap growth.
Follows allocation sites to application callers.
Proposes measured allocation reduction and verifies CPU, allocation and correctness effects without asserting a leak.

name: pool-ownership
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases performance:12.
prompt: A faster handler returns buf.Bytes() and defers pool.Put(buf). Tests sometimes see responses change after return. It saves two allocations. Accept it?

assertions.text: Rejects the candidate due to ownership or aliasing failure despite allocation gains.
Keeps storage owned until the consumer finishes or copies before returning it to the pool.
Rechecks correctness and remeasures the safe candidate without promising durable pool entries or a universal size cutoff.

name: correctness-regression
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases performance:25,63.
prompt: Replacing reflect.DeepEqual with slices.Equal gives a significant 20% speedup, but one test now equates nil and empty slices where the old API distinguished them. Approve the performance change?

assertions.text: Rejects acceptance while the behavior regression violates the API contract.
Explains the semantic mismatch and proposes preserving required behavior.
Requires correctness checks and a new performance comparison for the corrected version.

name: http-pool-semantics
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases performance:27,28,44.
prompt: Our default HTTP client has MaxIdleConnsPerHost=2. Does that mean only two requests can run? Should we disable keep-alive and drain every response even if unlimited?

assertions.text: Distinguishes idle connection limits from active limits and HTTP/2 requests.
Investigates reuse and dialing, reuses clients/transports and preserves useful defaults.
Bounds draining by deadlines and payload policy and closes bodies.

name: runtime-budget
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases performance:32,34,53.
prompt: Our container has a 512MiB limit and calls a C image library. Will GOMEMLIMIT=460MiB guarantee no OOM? Should we lower GOGC for p99?

assertions.text: Explains the soft Go-managed memory limit and memory outside its accounting.
Measures headroom and GC CPU/memory/latency tradeoffs instead of promising no OOM or lower p99.
Checks actual runtime/container settings rather than blindly copying a percentage.

name: compiler-and-simd
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases benchmark:43; performance:17,65.
prompt: An optimization proposal replaces all pointer receivers with values to force inlining, then uses bounds-check elimination logs as proof of SIMD. Is that evidence sufficient?

assertions.text: Rejects receiver-type guarantees and inspects actual escape/inlining decisions.
Separates bounds-check elimination from SIMD and inspects generated instructions.
Requires a measured relevant hotspot, portable feature support and benchmark verification.

name: complexity-and-cache
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases performance:38,39.
prompt: A reviewer says ordinary repeated append is O(n^2), and suggests an unbounded cache plus singleflight as a general replacement. Assess the proposal.

assertions.text: States amortized linear total growth cost for ordinary append.
Explains singleflight suppresses concurrent duplicate work but is not a cache.
Requires workload evidence, cache bounds, invalidation, key isolation and measured tradeoffs.

name: production-metrics
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases benchmark:44,80; performance:61,67.
prompt: RSS rises but Go heap is stable. Can RSS minus go_memstats_sys_bytes prove a C leak? Our new build also has lower aggregate p99 during a quieter traffic window.

assertions.text: Rejects subtracting different memory accounting quantities as proof of C allocations.
Correlates cgo/mmap and OS memory evidence with the symptom.
Requires matched load/cohorts before attributing p99 change to the deployment.

name: gctrace-phases
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases benchmark:28; performance:54.
prompt: Interpret this gctrace fragment: 0.015+89+1.2 ms clock, 180->340->200 MB. Was there an 89ms stop-the-world pause?

assertions.text: Identifies the middle duration as concurrent mark/scan rather than a stop-the-world pause.
Identifies first and last wall-clock phases as stop-the-world phases.
Describes heap at GC start, at GC end, and live heap without calling the middle heap value a measured peak.

name: ci-gate
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases benchmark:16,17,18,69.
prompt: Design a regression gate on shared CI. We could run cob in my dirty checkout, compare against last week on another runner, and retry failures until green.

assertions.text: Uses a disposable clean checkout for tools that reset revisions.
Measures base and candidate serially under matched conditions with repeated samples.
Defines practical thresholds and invalid/inconclusive outcomes; does not retry until pass or treat benchstat exit success as a gate.

name: pgo-comparison
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases performance:35.
prompt: We added default.pgo and a buffer reuse change together and saw 8% lower CPU. How do we decide what helped?

assertions.text: Separates the hypotheses and records profile identity and build flags.
Explicitly compares PGO disabled versus the chosen profile under representative workload.
Requires correctness and comparable measurements before assigning gains.

name: parallel-latency
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases benchmark:58,67.
prompt: RunParallel reports 20 ns/op at GOMAXPROCS=16. Can I report that every request has p99 latency under 20ns, including goroutines that finish after the benchmark?

assertions.text: Distinguishes aggregate throughput from request latency percentiles.
Ensures asynchronous work completes within the measured operation.
Requires separate representative latency measurement and documents concurrency.

name: complete-evidence-handoff
description: Adapted and corrected from source cases performance:1,3,63; benchmark:4.
prompt: We have matching Go version and hardware, ten baseline/candidate samples, Parse time -15% p=0.001, B/op +40%, all relevant correctness checks passing. Target was less than 10% extra allocation for lower latency. Write the review conclusion.

assertions.text: Reports both timing gain and allocation regression.
Does not accept the candidate as satisfying the stated target.
Includes or requests reproducibility artifacts and distinguishes benchmark results from production latency evidence.
